_comment: Contract A (§9.1) node ownership map. Each future engine's graph wave appends its node types. node_type strings are the CODE-LEVEL strings passed to assert_owner, not spec labels.

ownership._note: MARGIN is a PER-DIMENSION node (00-ENGINES-ROADMAP.md:234, the margin-trinity worked example for per-field ownership): 'signed'=Sales (frozen/immutable), 'estimated'=Project, 'actual'=Economy cascade. Only the 'actual' row is registered here — Economy owns just its own dimension. The 'signed' and 'estimated' rows are deliberately UNCLAIMED; they belong to Sales' and Project's own waves when built, not to Economy. Do NOT add a transition:null row for MARGIN — that would silently re-claim the whole node type and deny Sales/Project their dimensions (the Contract A bug this fixed in Batch 121 round-2).

Module 9's FIRST Contract-A row (Batch 142b). transition:null — Assets is the SOLE writer-of-record for the whole ASSET node, following the GOODS_RECEIPT / INVENTORY_RMA whole-node precedent above, NOT the per-transition MARGIN pattern (which is split because four engines write one node's status in sequence; nothing of the kind applies here). Without this row assert_owner's deny-by-default refuses every ASSET node write. Deliberately NOT added by this wave: FUNCTIONAL_LOCATION (owned by system_design, already registered above — Assets writes the lives_in EDGE to it and never authors the node) and BOM_LINE (Batch 132a / 133b's rows; Assets writes the installed_as edge by label only).

Batch 132a (Module 0, Wave 31): BOM_LINE is per-transition split, following the MARGIN pattern above, not the ASSET/GOODS_RECEIPT whole-node pattern — content is authored by whichever flow created the line (system_design for generated-from-design, sales for manual/package/external), content freezes at contract signature (content:freeze, sales-owned), and status advances independently through procurement → inventory → field_tech. TWELVE rows are registered at once (four content:create:{flow}, four content:update:{flow}, one content:freeze, three status:{state}) — the build plan's own text contradicts itself (§3/§6 say eight, §9 says five) and never resolves it; registering all twelve up front costs nothing because a row grants nothing until code calls with that exact transition (deny-by-default, proven by assert_owner's own mechanics), and it removes four future turns on this exclusive, count-test-free chokepoint. content:update:{flow} is NEW — the plan omitted it entirely. All of the plan's rows were content:create:* or content:freeze, but the store must be mutable pre-freeze (draft editing); without a content:update:{flow} row, an update call hits deny-by-default and pre-freeze editing is refused for every engine, including the line's own creator. NEVER add a transition:null row for BOM_LINE — Batch 121/MARGIN already shipped exactly that bug once (a null row silently re-claims every future, not-yet-registered transition for one engine, removing deny-by-default precisely where a brand-new flow gets added later without review).
